rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE A 'LOW CARBON ECONOMY' BY ESTABLISHING THE GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSION CAP, EMISSION REDUCTION OFF-SETTING, CREDITING, AND TRADE SYSTEM IN THE PHILIPPINES TO REDUCE GREEN HOUSE EMISSIONS AND MITIGATE THE ADVERSE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE
rows.abstract: Defines several key terms, including carbon credit or offset, climate change, emission cap/reduction/trading scheme, global warming, greenhouse gas, and the Paris Agreement on Climate Change. Proposes the implementation of greenhouse gas (GHG) emission caps on industrial and commercial establishments, individuals, and other entities that emit greenhouse gases. The specific limits will be determined by the DENR and the DOST. Entities will only be allowed to discharge a predetermined amount of specific greenhouse gases over a designated time period, with penalties for non-compliance. The proposal also encourages these entities to offset their GHG emissions by investing in and participating in GHG reduction projects which may include forestry initiatives, renewable energy projects, carbon dioxide capture and storage projects, and efforts to eliminate methane emissions. In return for their participation, these entities will receive GHG emission allowances, commonly referred to as "carbon credits." The proposal also seeks to establish a trading system that allows GHG emission allowances or carbon credits to be sold, exchanged, purchased, or traded by any individual or entity.
rows.status: Substituted by HB11375

rows.author: K005;K092;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE CARBON RIGHTS ACT, PROVIDING FOR THE OWNERSHIP, TRANSFER, AND BENEFIT-SHARING OF CARBON CREDITS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Refers "carbon rights" to the legal entitlements associated with the benefits derived from activities aimed at avoiding, reducing, or removing carbon emissions. These rights are related to the outcomes of such actions and are not classified as natural resources. Carbon rights encompass the ownership, transfer, and trading of carbon credits resulting from these activities. Defines "carbon project" as any initiative, activity, or program that leads to the reduction, removal, or avoidance of carbon dioxide (CO2) or other greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, thus generating carbon credits. Aims to establish a comprehensive, clear, and robust legal framework that will encourage private sector investments in carbon projects, which include: 1. Nature-Based Solutions (NBS) such as: - Afforestation, reforestation, and revegetation - Improved forest management - Reduced emissions from deforestation and forest degradation - Wetland restoration and conservation - Mangrove restoration - Soil carbon sequestration 2. Technology-Based Solutions, including: - Renewable energy projects - Energy efficiency projects - Carbon capture and storage - Waste management projects 3. Hybrid Projects, which integrate: - Renewable energy and agroforestry - Sustainable agriculture with biogas production. The framework will delineate carbon rights for Nature-Based Solutions (NBS) carbon projects applicable to: - Lands under public domain - Private lands and Indigenous Peoples' lands (ancestral domains) - Areas with overlapping jurisdictions. Additionally, the framework specifies the roles and mandates of various agencies, including the Climate Change Commission, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), the Department of Agriculture (DA), the Department of Energy (DOE), and the Department of Transportation (DOTr).

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR CHEAPER AND MORE ACCESSIBLE INTERNET FOR ALL
rows.title_short: Sana All May Internet Act
rows.abstract: Aims to establish a policy and regulation that shall reduce to zero the spectrum user fee (SUF) paid by telecommunications entities to the national government; promote the acceleration of internet use in the country, and the expansion of Wi-Fi technology and infrastructure in unserved and underserved areas; encourage and empower the small players in the industry to provide affordable internet services; and adopt a license-free, zero USF policy in accordance with international best practices.
